title: Mitsu Chem Plast Ltd - 540078 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 72.98% to INR1,422.74 lakh at a 16.45% margin, which management says is partly war-driven and sees ~10% as sustainable.
summary.overview: Mitsu Chem Plast reported Q4 FY26 total income of INR8,679.47 lakh, EBITDA of INR1,422.74 lakh (+72.98% YoY) and net profit of INR771.73 lakh (+117.90% YoY), with margins expanding on product mix and efficiency. For FY26, total income grew 5.40% to INR35,084.56 lakh while EBITDA rose 48.88% to INR3,466.31 lakh (9.90% margin). Management said it is prioritising bottom-line over top-line, with revenue growth muted, and guided to at least 30% growth in FY27. Management also announced entry into the IBC (Intermediate Bulk Container) vertical via a fully automated plant at Khalapur, with commissioning slated for Q2.

financial_highlights.value: As stated as 5.68% in transcript (likely INR 5.68)

segments.name: Packaging / containers (core)
segments.commentary: Management said about 84% of revenue comes from packaging items, with the 84:16 split expected to move to roughly 80:20 as Furnastra grows. Core business uses blow and injection moulding across 51 blow and 22 injection machines.

segments.name: Furnastra healthcare furniture and infra
segments.commentary: About 16% of revenue, with EBITDA margin stated at 15%+ and margin similar between furniture and infra. Management expects this share to reach 15-20% of the INR1,000 crore target, and a global supplier tie-up supports growth.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth guidance of minimum 30%; management said it is a planning figure and not backed by order book, and that the revenue rise would be partly price-led and partly volume-led.
Second-half weighting for FY27 growth, per analyst exchange on implied quarterly run-rate of about INR100-110 crore.
EBITDA margin: management called 10% the minimum sustainable level and said internal targets are a little above 10%.
Long-term aspiration of INR1,000 crore annual revenue by FY28, with capex needed to get there (amount not yet announced).
IBC plant to start production in Q2 FY27; detailed capacity, margin and ROCE details to be shared at Q2.
Capex for FY27 to be announced soon; no figure given.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity exceeds 29,900 metric tons per year across Maharashtra facilities, with 51 blow moulding and 22 injection moulding machines.
Unit 4 has already started; further expansion and operational efficiency gains expected in FY27.
IBC: fully automated plant at Khalapur facility, production start guided for Q2 FY27; capacity not disclosed.
Tarapur unit started; infrastructure ready for Boisar and Tarapur expansion.
Management said ready infrastructure (land, buildings) exists, but capex will be needed to reach INR1,000 crore.
Fixed asset turnover targeted at around 4 to 5x at normal utilisation; current average stated as 3.70x (analyst had cited 1.70x). Minimum utilisation of 40-45% to avoid margin dilution.
demand_pricing: Main raw material is HDPE (other materials also used). HDPE prices rose about 40% after the war, and management said they have eased to about 30%.
Customer pricing is a mix of monthly contracts and spot contracts; spot contracts were used during the war spike.
Management said Q4 margin had a 1-2 percentage point benefit from the raw material spike, and that this could reverse.
Exports now span more than 17 countries across pharma, healthcare, chemical and FMCG; Furnastra supplies parts to a global hospital-bed supplier (three to four designs approved).
Management added more than 175 customers in the last year, focusing on better margins; revenue was partly sacrificed for unprofitable sales.
Management declined to comment on competitor margins when asked about the gap with a peer at around 15% EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 EBITDA margin jump, and what is the sustainable margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited value addition and efficiency since Q3, plus a 1-2 point benefit from the war-driven raw material spike. Management called 9-10% fair, with 10% the minimum and internal targets a bit higher.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 growth target and is it volume or revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Minimum 30% growth, described as both revenue and volume. Management said it is a planning figure, not order-book backed, since orders typically cover only about a month.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Furnastra mix and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Furniture and infra about 16% of revenue, packaging 84%. Furnastra EBITDA margin stated at 15%+; furniture and infra margins are about the same.

qa_highlights.question: Will IBC margins exceed current container margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IBC should earn better margins because few players are in it, but would not quantify and will share details at Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the target fixed asset turnover and hurdle rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed asset turnover is targeted at 4-5x at normal utilisation, and management said it will be above 4x. No hurdle rate was given; IBC details to come at Q2. Minimum utilisation of 40-45% was cited.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to INR1,000 crore revenue and what capex is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Hospital and infra expected at 15-20% of the INR1,000 crore mix, with containers and packaging the rest. Capex will be needed but was not quantified; management said it will be announced step by step.

risks_watch: Raw material (HDPE) price volatility and possible reversal of Q4 inventory gains; management said the benefit could reverse.
Q4 margin (16.45%) is well above management's stated 10% sustainable level; watch whether Q1 FY27 margins normalise.
FY27 30% growth guidance has no disclosed order-book support and is weighted to H2.
Capex for FY27 not yet quantified; IBC capacity, margin and ROCE hurdle undisclosed until Q2.
Management was evasive on competitor margin comparison and on incremental ROCE hurdle.
Furnastra export volumes depend on customer approvals (six to twelve months in some countries).
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and long-term ambition, but cautious and often evasive on specifics: capex, IBC capacity, hurdle rate and peer comparisons were deferred to Q2. Management was candid that the quarter had a war-related raw material benefit.
key_quotes: And some part, the extra margin has come up from maybe the war situation, which has happened.
So I think double-digit is -- Q3 also was double-digit. And I think we consider that 9% to 10% is fair enough in our business.
Much, much better than this. I think minimum, minimum 30% growth this year, minimum.

adds.what: IBC (Intermediate Bulk Container) fully automated plant at Khalapur facility; capacity not disclosed
Tarapur unit started; infrastructure ready for Boisar and Tarapur expansion (no capex or capacity figure)

growth.why: Management guides minimum 30% FY27 revenue growth (partly price-led, partly volume-led) but calls it a planning figure not backed by order book; capacity backing is limited to the IBC plant (capacity undisclosed, Q2 FY27 start) and an unquantified Tarapur/Boisar expansion with capex not yet announced.
